content.title: About
content.content: Grilled chicken fillet is a tender, skinless piece of lean meat cooked over an open flame. It has a light smoky aroma, juicy texture, and a mildly salty flavor. Perfect for salads, sandwiches, Asian‑style dishes, and quick weeknight meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grilling preserves most of the protein and vitamins compared with deep‑frying.
Chicken fillet is one of the most affordable sources of high‑quality protein.
Proper marinating can boost flavor without adding extra salt.
The grill allows excess fat to drip away, reducing overall fat content.
In many cuisines grilled chicken is served with chimichurri, teriyaki, or lemon‑herb sauces.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Chicken fillet provides about 31 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Skinless and grilled, it contains only 3–4 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies niacin (B3), vitamin B6, and B12, which are essential for metabolism and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Chicken fillet offers iron, zinc, and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The high protein content helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Undercooked chicken may harbor salmonella; cook to an internal temperature of 75 °C (165 °F).

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to chicken proteins.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: When using salty marinades, monitor overall sodium intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice grilled chicken fillet for salads, add to sandwiches, serve with vegetable sides, or toss into pasta. It stores well in the fridge for 3‑4 days and can be reheated or eaten cold.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the fillet to room temperature, then place in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 4 days. For longer storage, freeze in bags at –18 °C (0 °F) where it retains quality for up to 2 months.

chocolate-candy-nougat-filled-with-nuts.title: Chocolate candy, nougat filled with nuts

content.title: About
content.content: Chocolate candy with nougat filled with nuts is a sweet treat where a soft, nut‑laden nougat center is coated with a thin layer of milk or dark chocolate. The candy offers a creamy, sweet flavor, a hint of nutty richness, and a pleasant crunch from the nuts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nougat originated in the Mediterranean during the Middle Ages, originally made from honey, egg whites, and nuts.
These candies often combine hazelnuts, almonds, and cashews for a richer taste profile.
In some countries the shape resembles a “tube,” giving rise to a colloquial name.
Manufacturers frequently add vanilla or sea salt to accentuate the sweet‑salty contrast.
The combination of chocolate and nuts is believed to enhance the perception of flavor depth.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: The nut filling provides monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Chocolate, especially dark, contains flavonoids that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Nuts supply magnesium, phosphorus, and iron, important for muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides sustained energy
items.content: The blend of carbohydrates from the nougat and fats from the nuts offers lasting satiety and energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Nougat and nuts contain vitamins B1, B2, and B6, which play roles in metabolism.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: These candies can trigger severe allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to nuts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Nougat and chocolate make the product calorie‑dense and rich in simple sugars; moderation is key.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: A single serving may contain 150–250 kcal, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Caffeine content
items.content: Dark chocolate contains small amounts of caffeine, which may be undesirable for children.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the candies as a standalone dessert, stir them into ice cream, incorporate into baked goods, or use as a garnish for cakes. They also make a convenient on‑the‑go energy bite.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the candies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to prevent chocolate bloom.

content.title: About
content.content: Pompano is a marine fish from the family Carangidae, found in warm coastal waters of the Atlantic and Pacific oceans. When baked or broiled with a coating, it offers tender white flesh, a mildly sweet flavor, and a crisp crust.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pompano is often called the “golden fish” because of its golden‑hued skin.
It is a staple in Caribbean and Southeast Asian cuisines.
In the wild, pompano can reach up to 70 cm in length and weigh about 4 kg.
The flesh is rich in omega‑3 fatty acids, beneficial for heart health.
Proper coating techniques keep the crust crunchy even after baking.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids help lower triglyceride levels and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100‑g serving provides about 20 g of complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pompano supplies vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: It contains selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, supporting immune function and bone health.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: Compared with red meat, pompano has low saturated fat, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to seafood, including pompano.

items.title: Heavy‑metal contamination
items.content: Like many marine fish, pompano can accumulate mercury; moderate consumption is advised, especially for children and pregnant women.

items.title: Overconsumption
items.content: Large portions may lead to excess calories and fat intake despite the fish’s healthy profile.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Bake the fish at 180 °C for 12‑15 minutes after coating it in breadcrumbs, spices, and a drizzle of olive oil. For pan‑searing, cook 3‑4 minutes per side until golden. Serve with lemon wedges, fresh herbs, and a light vegetable side.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh pompano refrigerated at 0‑2 °C, wrapped in plastic film, and use within 2 days. Frozen fish can be stored up to 3 months at –18 °C. Before cooking, check for a fresh sea scent; a strong ammonia odor indicates spoilage.
